one_line: New export controls and memory shortages disrupt global AI hardware supply chains as regulatory scrutiny intensifies around Nvidia and Character.ai.

themes.title: Export controls and memory shortages squeeze hardware
themes.text: New U.S. export restrictions have halted AI server shipments to Southeast Asian countries and stalled billions in data center loans tied to Chinese firms. Meanwhile, global memory chip shortages are driving up prices tenfold and pushing B300 chip delivery wait times to 40 weeks.

stories.headline: US chip curbs stall billions in data center loans tied to Chinese firms
Nvidia stops shipping AI servers to four Southeast Asian countries
Memory chip shortages spark global procurement war rooms and 10x price hikes
NVIDIA B300 AI chip orders face up to 40‑week wait; RTX 60 GPU may slip past 2027

themes.title: Nvidia faces credit and political pressure
themes.text: S&P Global Ratings is considering a credit downgrade for Nvidia following management stability concerns, while Pentagon officials discussed leveraging the Defense Production Act over CEO Jensen Huang's role. Nvidia is also facing ongoing investigations regarding alleged chip smuggling to China by a customer.

stories.headline: Pentagon officials discussed using Defense Production Act over Nvidia CEO role
S&P considers Nvidia credit downgrade over governance risks
Nvidia faces ongoing investigations over Megaspeed chip smuggling after CEO’s return

themes.title: States challenge data auctions and toy sales
themes.text: A coalition of 42 state attorneys general is attempting to block Character.ai’s planned auction of private chat data from over 21 million accounts. Additionally, New York Governor Kathy Hochul signed a five-year ban on AI chatbot toys, following a similar move by California.

stories.headline: 42 state attorneys general challenge Character.ai plan to auction private chats
New York governor signs five-year ban on AI chatbot toys

themes.title: Space data centers and infrastructure funding
themes.text: The FCC has authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million Starmind satellites intended to serve as data centers in space by 2040. In parallel, Nexent Capital launched a $1 billion fund aimed at quantum-ready AI infrastructure and energy projects.

stories.headline: US FCC authorizes SpaceX to deploy 1 million Starmind AI satellites
Nexent Capital launches $1 billion fund for AI data‑center and energy infrastructure
